summary: Preview of the USMNT friendly against Germany, the first match for new Germany head coach Julian Nagelsmann after Hansi Flick's exit following a second straight World Cup group-stage elimination. The article covers Nagelsmann's 26-man squad, likely lineups, his tactical style (4-2-3-1 and 3-2-4-1, Red Bull-style press), and open questions such as the lack of natural right-backs. It also reports German criticism of the DFB's travel to the US and Mexico.
one_line: Preview of Germany's friendly against the USMNT, Julian Nagelsmann's first match in charge, covering his squad, tactics and the criticized North America trip.
key_facts: Germany were eliminated in the group stage of two straight World Cups; before 2018 they had never been bounced from a World Cup that early.
Julian Nagelsmann, 36, replaced Hansi Flick as Germany head coach after the Qatar World Cup.
Nagelsmann spent three seasons at Hoffenheim and two years at RB Leipzig before taking the Bayern Munich job in 2021.
Nagelsmann won the Bundesliga title with Bayern in his first season but was sacked in March 2023 when Bayern sat a point behind Dortmund.
His 26-man squad includes five Bayern Munich players, among them Josh Kimmich and Leon Goretzka.
The squad has five center-backs but only two natural full-backs, David Raum and Robin Gosens, both left-sided, and no natural right-backs.
Mats Hummels was recalled, having not been called up since 2021 and been left out throughout Flick's time in charge.
Kevin Behrens, Chris Fuhrich and Robert Andrich received first national team call-ups.
Serge Gnabry is out with a broken arm, and Timo Werner has a back problem at RB Leipzig.
Predicted XI in a 4-2-3-1: ter Stegen; Kimmich, Rudiger, Sule, Raum; Gundogan, Goretzka; Sane, Musiala, Brandt; Fullkrug.
Late in 2022/23 Nagelsmann switched Bayern from a 4-2-3-1 to a 3-2-4-1, which Guardiola, Pioli, Arteta and Terzic have also used.
Jamal Musiala, 20, has just one goal in 23 international caps; Thomas Muller has 123 caps and 45 goals.
Germany return to Europe a single day before Dortmund's October 20 match against Werder Bremen, drawing criticism of the travel schedule.
Bayern manager Thomas Tuchel and Lothar Matthaus both questioned the trip to the USA and Mexico before the Euros in Germany.
